records.description: Use purified mature DM-MBP V8G/Y283D, normally100 nM at 25 C, plus concentration-series and wild-type controls. The chloride-containing arm dilutes100-fold from 6 M guanidine-HCl into 20 mM Tris-HCl pH7.5,200 mM KCl and 5 mM Mg(OAc)2. The chloride-deficient arm dilutes100-fold from 9.5 M urea into 100 mM Hepes pH7.5,20 mM KOAc and 5 mM Mg(OAc)2. In each chaperonin arm capture with 250 nM GroEL or SR1, then add 250 nM GroES and 5 mM ATP. Record tryptophan fluorescence at 295 nm excitation/345 nm emission and separate dynamic light scattering. The two solution protocols differ in several components.
records.name: Purified DM-MBP refolding and aggregation context
openObligations: Purified, already synthesized clients and purified E. coli GroEL/SR1/GroES are studied in vitro. The selected data do not observe translation, cellular stress adaptation, protein damage surveillance, routing to proteasomes or organismal proteome reliability.

Adding the GroEL/GroES/ATP protocol is a combined intervention. These panels do not by themselves isolate ATP hydrolysis, individual ATPase steps, capture specificity, every component necessity or all possible active folding effects.

Activity recovery, tryptophan fluorescence, light scattering and size-exclusion elution measure different properties. None alone supplies an atomic native structure, a unique folding path or the fraction of every chain in a single native state.
All readouts and fitted rates come from one publication. No raw traces, new fit, covariance, curve digitization, independent replication or analytically-checked status is supplied.

The source interprets these conditions through aggregation prevention. Its broad passive-cage conclusion is retained as conditional, not a proof that all chaperonins are passive or that no client can experience an active conformational effect.

The DM-MBP client is mature V8G/Y283D maltose-binding protein. Tryptophan fluorescence is an environment-sensitive refolding proxy; no maltose-binding affinity, transport activity or enzymatic client assay is measured here.

The chloride-containing protocol uses 20 mM Tris-HCl pH7.5,200 mM KCl and 5 mM Mg(OAc)2 after dilution from 6 M guanidine-HCl. The chloride-deficient protocol uses 100 mM Hepes pH7.5,20 mM KOAc and 5 mM Mg(OAc)2 after dilution from 9.5 M urea. Buffer, salt concentration/anion and starting denaturant all change; chloride alone is not isolated.

Concentration dependence and light scattering support intermolecular association under the tested solution protocol. They do not identify a unique oligomer structure or prove that every fluorescence intermediate is an aggregate.

Rate equivalence in the changed solution protocol constrains a need for a faster intrinsic cage-only step for this client under those conditions. It does not prove an unchanged microscopic route or universal absence of chaperonin active effects.

openObligations: The complete actual published article pages 1229-1232 and complete PMC author main text were read. The published version has three figures, whereas the longer author manuscript has five; locators retain both mappings. The published PDF also contains portions of unrelated adjacent articles, which supply no evidence here.

The Supporting Online Material was not read: direct archive endpoints returned small HTML challenges and publisher access failed. Complete RNA preparation, calibration, background/no-enzyme controls, replicate definitions and supplementary figures S1-S2 are not reconstructed. Main-text assay details and its observed finite transfer series are the admitted boundary.

The catalysts are RNA ligases supplied as a starting seed and assembled from supplied sequence-specific oligoribonucleotide fragments with activated 5-prime triphosphates. This is not nucleotide-by-nucleotide copying, arbitrary genome replication, de novo nucleotide/fragment synthesis, or self-production of every resource.

The pair assay contains no proteins during amplification. Prior laboratory synthesis/evolution/preparation can use biological machinery; absence of proteins in the amplification vessel does not mean the entire experimental production history was protein-free.

A denaturing gel separates labeled substrates and full-length ligation products; the source fits product accumulation to a logistic growth model. That fit and the reciprocal reaction topology support finite cross-catalytic amplification, not an independently reconstructed fold/tertiary structure or proof of every catalytic-closure axiom of an arbitrary RAF network.

Single-batch growth levels off as substrates are depleted. Six successive five-hour incubations with 4 percent carryover and fresh substrate demonstrate 30 hours of operation; the reported cumulative amplification greater than 10^8 accounts for serial dilution and is not the final vessel concentration. Indefinite continuation is conditional extrapolation beyond the observed series.

The mixed population is a different preparation with 15 mM rather than 25 mM MgCl2, many supplied substrates and 5 percent transfer. Its finite 100-hour result is read but not a second independent publication or the same paired-assay context. It is not admitted here as open-ended evolution or a new arbitrary-function genetic system.

No protein-folding prerequisite, universal protein catalytic ancestry, site cooperativity, allosteric feedback, physical compartment requirement, spontaneous prebiotic origin, unrestricted food generation, living autonomy or universal network persistence is established.
No raw gel acquisition, independent fit, isotope/radiolabel calibration, numerical replay, experimental replication or new experimental optimization was performed.
